questions.note: Order is right in V1f, V3 and V5f: hallux longest, 2nd a few mm shorter, 3–5 descending; hallux ≈31 mm across (≈460 px at 14.7 px/mm), toe 2 ≈16 mm. But toes 2–4 are near-identical smooth tubes with soft knuckles, faint IP wrinkles and round glossy pulps, and the 5th stands beside the 4th with a gap rather than tucked under it.

Five left nails present, trimmed straight, with a free edge (hallux ≈19 mm chord in V5f, edge ≈0.7 mm in hr.hallux). But the plates sit on the skin with a white rim at base and sides instead of passing under the folds; no lunula reads, no pink bed or onychodermal band, glossy hotspots; the lesser nails are copies of one shape.

Extensor slips to toes 2–5 and a ridge toward the hallux catch the light as low relief, but as thin even lines (≈1–1.5 mm at 11 px/mm) where cords of 3.5–5 mm belong. No dorsal venous arch, no tributaries, no great saphenous in front of the medial malleolus in V1f, V2 or the zoom: half of what the question asks is absent.

No waxy glow: the toes' shadow sides stay dark. Micro-relief exists (fine cells on the hallux at 43 px/mm, plantar ridges at ≈0.45 mm pitch) but the ridges are identical bullseyes with a seam, the dorsum is blotchy noise without zoning, toes and pulps are smooth and silicone-like, the heel callus is a crackle decal, and the nails have plastic hotspots.

defects.what: No dorsal veins: no venous arch across the dorsum at 55–65 % L, no tributaries, and (in V2) no great saphenous in front of the medial malleolus; only straight tendon lines break the smooth dorsum.
defects.fix: Build the dorsal venous arch with 2–4 meandering, branching tributaries, 2.5–3 mm across and 0.7 mm proud, draining into a 3–3.5 mm great saphenous 1 mm proud in front of the medial malleolus, tinted grey-green.

defects.what: No Achilles tendon or retro-malleolar hollows: from z ≈ 40 to 100 mm the back of the ankle is one broad convex surface with a faint central highlight; nothing narrows into the heel and nothing dips beside the malleoli.
defects.fix: Raise a cord 16 mm wide and 7 mm deep that narrows to its insertion at z ≈ 52, with hollows 4 mm deep (the pre-Achilles fat pads) between it and each malleolus.

defects.what: Hallux nail reads as a stuck-on acrylic tip: a white rim shows along its base and sides instead of the plate passing under the folds; no cuticle, no lunula reads, an even beige plate with no pink bed or onychodermal band, glossy hotspots.
defects.fix: Tuck the plate's base 4–5 mm under the eponychium with a thin cuticle over it, sink its sides into the lateral grooves, show a soft 3.5 mm lunula, a pink bed through the plate and a narrow onychodermal band; satin, not varnished.

defects.what: The heel callus covers the whole plantar heel pad (≈67 × 37 mm at 4.6 px/mm) and ends forward in a ruler-straight transverse edge, a visible mask boundary.
defects.fix: Keep the thick callus to a 12–18 mm band round the posterior and lateral rim, fading over 5–10 mm into the pinker weight-bearing heel centre with its friction ridges; no straight edge anywhere.

defects.what: Callus fissures are a regular net of thin, dark, closed polygons on chalky grey-white skin along the heel rim; it reads as crackle glaze, dried mud or grime rather than callus.
defects.fix: Real callus crazing is pale, with white scaly edges, irregular and fading inward, plus a few deeper radial fissures 0.3–0.8 mm wide with pale lips and pink-brown floors, on yellowish, waxy, matte callus.

defects.what: Toes 2–5 are smooth tubes with soft knuckles: almost no transverse wrinkles over the PIP and DIP joints, smooth skin up to the nail folds, round glossy pulps; they read young and rubbery.
defects.fix: Real toes narrow between the joints, with defined dorsal knuckles, 3–6 transverse wrinkles 0.2 mm deep over each IP joint, fine lines above each nail fold, and drier, duller pulps.

defects.what: Nails of toes 2–4 are scaled copies of one rounded plate with the same thin white free-edge line and crisp outline; the 5th is a clean miniature of them, not a small, thickened, ridged nail.
defects.fix: Give each lesser nail its own outline, curvature and edge: narrower and more curved than the hallux's, partly hidden by the folds, unevenly trimmed; the 5th small, 0.9 mm thick, ridged and turned outward.

defects.what: No 5th metatarsal tuberosity: the lateral border runs smooth from the heel to the 5th MTP with no bump at mid-foot, about 150 mm from the heel (≈900 px from it at 6 px/mm).
defects.fix: Add the styloid, 8 mm across and 2.5 mm proud, at (+50, −150, 18), with the lateral border dipping slightly in front of it.

defects.what: The medial arch is low and straight when standing: the plantar border clears the floor by about 6 mm (≈40 px at 6 px/mm) along a flat ramp from heel to ball; no navicular tuberosity shows.
defects.fix: Shape the medial border as an arch peaking under the navicular, with the 12 mm tuberosity 2 mm proud at about z 42 and the abductor hallucis fullness below it.

defects.what: The skin is one peach tone with large blotchy noise (5–10 mm blobs) over the dorsum, ankle and heel, with no anatomical colour zoning.
defects.fix: Zone it: redder toes and knuckles, grey-green over the veins, paler yellow plantar margins rising onto the sides, browner creases at the ankle; keep variation at freckle and capillary scale, not large blobs.

defects.what: Callus only at the heel: the ball under MT heads 1–2 is pink and evenly ridged with no pale flattened patch; no boot-rub callus at the 5th MTP, no pinch callus on the medial hallux IP, no corn on the 4th toe.
defects.fix: Add callus 2 (32 × 22 mm under MT1–2, ridges flattened), callus 3 (Ø 18 mm at the 5th MTP, wrapping onto the border), callus 4 (14 × 10 mm at the medial hallux IP) and the 5 mm dorsal corn on toe 4's PIP.

defects.what: Extensor tendons are thin, even, straight lines about 1–1.5 mm wide (≈12–16 px at 11 px/mm); the EHL is not distinct from the fan to toes 2–5.
defects.fix: Make the EHL a 5 mm cord 1.5 mm proud and the EDL slips 3.5 mm wide and 1 mm proud, rounded in section and fading in and out over the MT heads.

defects.what: Pulp friction ridges are perfect concentric bullseyes, evenly spaced and the same on every toe, with no ridge endings, forks, pores, deltas or white lines.
defects.fix: Real dermatoglyphs are irregular loops and whorls with deltas, ridge endings and forks every few mm, pores along the ridges, and fine creases crossing them on an adult sole.

defects.what: Flexion creases on toes 3 and 4 are ruler-straight black cuts across the toe, and the clefts between the touching lesser toes are hairline black slits like mesh seams.
defects.fix: Digital creases are curved, soft-edged folds about 0.5 mm deep with the ridges running into them; touching toes meet in a rounded, shadowed groove.

defects.what: A straight seam runs from the hallux IP crease into the whorl centre with the ridges mismatched across it; the same line runs down toe 3's pad.
defects.fix: Let the ridges flow continuously across the pad, with no discontinuity.

defects.what: Jagged brownish arcs at the bases of toes 2–4 on the sole mark a texture-zone boundary with a torn edge, not a crease.
defects.fix: Blend the sole and toe colour zones over several mm and put the digito-plantar crease there as a soft fold.

defects.what: The hallux tuft (and the toe hairs) read as short, straight, parallel dark dashes, like scratches in the skin rather than fine hairs.
defects.fix: 8–12 hairs 5–8 mm long tapering from 0.035 to 0.02 mm, gently curved and lying flat toward the tip with 10–20° random yaw.

ranked: [D1] No dorsal veins anywhere: no venous arch across the dorsum, no tributaries, no great saphenous in front of the medial malleolus. A lean 40-year-old soldier's foot shows them as raised, branching cords; without them the whole foot reads young and mannequin-smooth.

[D2] The back of the ankle is a smooth column: no Achilles cord narrowing into the heel and no hollows between it and the malleoli, so from behind and from either side the ankle reads like a cast or a stuffed stocking.

[D3] The hallux nail reads as a stuck-on acrylic tip: an even, glossy plate whose white rim shows at its base and sides, no cuticle, no lunula, no pink bed or onychodermal band. A real plate slides under the proximal fold and sinks into its side grooves.

[D4] On the sole the heel callus covers the whole heel pad and stops at a ruler-straight transverse line, a mask edge. Real callus is thickest at the posterior-lateral rim and feathers out into the pinker weight-bearing centre.

[D5] The callus cracks are a regular net of thin dark closed polygons on chalky grey-white skin, which reads as crackle glaze, dried mud or grime. Real heel callus is yellowish and waxy, its crazing pale and scaly, with a few radial fissures on the rim.

[D6] Toes 2–5 are smooth tubes: soft knuckles, almost no transverse wrinkles over the PIP and DIP joints, smooth skin right up to the nail folds, round glossy pulps. A boot-wearer of 40 has knobbly, creased toes that narrow between the joints.

[D7] The lesser nails are scaled copies of one rounded plate with the same thin white free edge. Real lesser toenails differ toe to toe: narrower, more curved, half-hidden by the folds, unevenly trimmed, and the 5th small, thick and ridged.
[D8] No 5th metatarsal tuberosity: the lateral border runs smooth from heel to the 5th MTP with no bump at mid-foot, though it is one of the most visible landmarks of a real lateral foot.

The lateral malleolus reads from the side only as a soft swelling, with no crisp lower tip, no sinus tarsi hollow in front of it and no peroneal groove behind it; V8 shows it about 5 mm proud, so it is the modelling around it that is too soft.

[D9] The medial arch is low and straight when standing: the plantar border clears the floor by about 6 mm as a flat ramp from heel to ball, with no navicular bump. A normal arch rises to a peak under the navicular.

[D10] The skin is one peach tone under large blotchy noise (5–10 mm blobs) everywhere. A real foot is zoned: redder toes and knuckles, a grey-green cast over veins, paler yellow plantar margins, browner creases at the ankle.

[D11] Callus only at the heel: no pale flattened patch under MT heads 1–2, no boot-rub callus at the 5th MTP, no pinch callus on the medial hallux IP, no corn on toe 4. The forefoot looks unworn for a man who lives in boots.

[D12] The extensor tendons are thin, even, straight lines about 1–1.5 mm wide fanning from the ankle. Real tendons are 3.5–5 mm cords that rise and fade along their course, with the EHL to the hallux clearly the strongest.
The front of the ankle has no transverse crease or fine parallel lines at the dorsiflexion line; a real ankle at rest shows at least one soft fold there.
The 5th toe stands apart from the 4th with an open gap and its nail facing mostly up. A boot-wearer's 5th toe is usually rolled further, nail facing outward, and pressed against or under the 4th.

[D13] The plantar friction ridges are perfect concentric bullseyes, the same on every pulp, with no breaks, forks, pores or white lines. Real dermatoglyphs are irregular loops and whorls with deltas, and an adult sole is crossed by fine creases.

[D14] The flexion creases on toes 3 and 4 are ruler-straight black cuts, and the clefts between touching lesser toes are hairline black slits. Real creases are curved, soft folds; touching toes meet in shadowed grooves.
[D15] A straight seam runs from the hallux's IP crease into the pad's whorl centre with the ridges mismatched across it; toe 3's pad has the same line.
[D16] Jagged brownish arcs at the toe bases on the sole mark where two texture zones meet; they read as a torn decal edge, not a crease.
[D17] The hallux tuft and the toe hairs are short, straight, parallel dark dashes, like scratches in the skin, not fine curved hairs lying flat toward the tips.
